Initial two-process phase created one reminder per task in one ordinary batch. Main reviewed original code and SQL state; continuation revalidated those effects, real receipt replay and two competing processes consuming a duplicate without another effect.

Initial hard-kill recovery failed its 180-second deadline. The pg adapter discarded multi-statement results; supervisor monitoring stopped before expiry recovery. Fixed normalization matches the pinned SDK behavior.

A later continuation reused the same pending logical task via explicit activation, then killed its own newly stalled process; production 60-second heartbeat/monitor recovered in 68.895 seconds with one result. No deadline or fake-clock relaxation.
Only the final two tasks were added in the last continuation. Total worker starts were 18 across fault scenarios; no more than two ran concurrently.

Active-job encrypted backup restored to one new empty database with framework schema 42, business/ciphertext parity and paused rotated generation; a restarted restored worker produced no business effect.
